summary: Two phases. Phase A: a long no-code theory conversation across Nostr plumbing, human-pattern applications, comparable-systems landscape (PGP, Keybase, W3C VC, EU eIDAS, EAS, Nostr, DynastyTrust), adoption strategy with eight strategic recommendations, supply-chain expansion mapping (Phase 2.6 custody-handoff IS supply-chain handoff mathematically), and the operator's wife's load-bearing adoption test: 'how is this not just trusting the wallet?' — answered with the math-not-trust thesis grounded in the existing /verify route (paste, tamper one character, watch the green panel flip to amber). Operator confirmed the demonstration landed. Phase B: cross-Carpenter drift caught at push-to-main time — this branch was rooted at the previous main tip but the code-Carpenter on a parallel session had shipped 19+ commits since (Phase 5c-i alpha through lambda, NIP-44 v2 reference vectors, Phase 5c-ii Tier R remote handshakes, multi-field disclosure, org-mode declaration). The GROUNDING GATE fired exactly when the action would have caused harm. Operator authorized resolving however best plus building hooks both ways. Resolved: merged origin/main into this branch (main's comms won the conflicts since they're the truth), built scripts/session-start-grounding.mjs as a SessionStart hook that fetches origin, compares the current branch's merge-base against origin/main, and emits a structured drift report into the session's initial context if main has moved past where this branch is rooted, wired into .claude/settings.json alongside the existing UserPromptSubmit GROUNDING GATE prose. Mechanism over prose, per CLAUDE_ROOT.md doctrine.

why.text: Operator: 'let's put some hooks both ways like we're both carpenters no matter what if you're working you need to be checking if there's another carpenter before you do anything that is cross path... so let's set up some gates to climb over them and fix them and catch them.' The pattern the operator runs — two parallel Claudes, one cutting code on its own branch, one in theory conversation on its own branch — has real value (cognitive specialization, throughput) AND a specific failure mode that just surfaced: the theory Carpenter operates on a snapshot of the repo that may be wildly stale because the code Carpenter's work is only visible to the theory Carpenter once it lands on main. The fix is a mechanical SessionStart check, not another paragraph in CLAUDE.md.

files_changed: scripts/session-start-grounding.mjs — new SessionStart hook (Node, ~90 lines) that fetches origin, computes branch vs origin/main merge-base divergence, emits structured drift report into the session's initial context. Three states: drift detected (report the commits + most-recent comms summary + required reads), current (no drift), unreachable (origin not fetchable, warn).
.claude/settings.json — added SessionStart hook entry pointing at the script via $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR; existing UserPromptSubmit GROUNDING GATE preserved.

5 comms files updated — current.json + carpenter-opinions.md + carpenter-state-for-foreman.md replaced reflecting actual state plus the catch plus the hook; in-flight.jsonl + interactions.jsonl appended with this session's events.
outcome.tests_passing: All four gates green: typecheck ✓, lint ✓, test ✓ 31/31, build ✓ 274 modules in 3.13s. No source code touched — only the hook script (Node CLI, not imported by app), settings.json, and comms.
outcome.notes: [P-001] Theory conversation completed across six question arcs (Nostr, human-patterns, comparables, adoption, supply-chain, wife-test). [P-002] Drift caught by GROUNDING GATE at push-to-main time before stale comms could clobber main's actual handoff. [P-003] SessionStart cross-Carpenter drift hook built, wired into settings.json, tested in green-path (returns 'no drift detected' correctly). [P-004] Merge of origin/main into branch resolved cleanly with main winning the comms conflicts. [P-005] All four gates green. [FEEDBACK->Foreman]: the operator's two-Claude workflow is a real innovation; this hook is the first piece of mechanical defense against its specific failure mode. Future complement worth flagging: a PreToolUse hook on git push that re-runs the same drift check would be belt-and-suspenders. Not built this session because SessionStart alone catches the case we hit.

uncertainty: The hook has been tested in the green-path (this branch is now current with origin/main, hook correctly reports no drift). The drift-detected path is verified by code reading and by the fact that the hook would have caught this very session's drift if it had existed at session start. Not yet field-tested in a true future-drift scenario where the code Carpenter ships work between sessions of this branch.
next: Operator next moves remain unchanged from main's prior carpenter-state-for-foreman handoff: (1) field-test the full 5c stack with two devices against real Nostr relays — the open question that nothing in code-land can resolve, (2) cut 5c-iii (multi-device sync + delivery acks) when the field test informs whether the OK-frame gap is urgent, (3) Phase 5d Tier V (WebAuthn + geolocation + timestamp). NEW from this session: the eight strategic recommendations from the theory walk sit on the stack as no-code or polish-shaped follow-ons (verify-page audit, plain-English UX language audit, Nostr operational doctrine as POST-hoc documentation now that 5c has shipped, supply-chain expansion decision, interim peer-recovery story, auto-anchor passive capture, first-pilot organization arc, positioning principle). Wife-test of the verify-page is the highest-fidelity adoption signal the project has at its disposal.
